hold_reason: The pinned lemma uses the Stacks definition of an immersion: a CLOSED immersion followed by an OPEN immersion. The proposed final statement instead defines an immersion as factorable by an OPEN immersion followed by a CLOSED immersion. These are not equivalent for arbitrary schemes (Stacks Schemes Definition 26.10.2 and Remark 26.10.3, including Morphisms Example 29.3.4), so the proposed biconditional wrongly substitutes a stricter property.
proposed_correction: Replace the parenthetical with 'factorable as a closed immersion followed by an open immersion', or remove it and refer to the Stacks definition of immersion. Require fresh independent source-first approval of the corrected statement.

final_content.statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism and $\{g_i:Y_i\to Y\}$ an fppf covering. Then $f$ is dominant (its set-theoretic image is dense in $Y$) if and only if every base-changed morphism $f_i:X\times_YY_i\to Y_i$ is dominant.
hypotheses: f:X→Y and an fppf covering of Y.
conclusions: Dominance is fppf-local on the target.

semantic_review_note: Pinned descent.tex L6346 states dominance is fppf-local on the TARGET. The reconstructed condition that the set-theoretic image is dense in Y and that the same holds after each member of an fppf target-cover preserves both directions. It does not require f to be surjective, and makes no incorrect claim about arbitrary non-flat base change.
